dataflow.outcome: credential and document bytes can reach a recipient different from the accepted declaration
dataflow.source: operator-controlled markdown adapter declaration containing target fields and authentication
dataflow.summary: accepted `tools.toml` target/auth -> `declared_adapter_for_role()` keeps auth/model but drops target -> `run_standard_online_markdownize()` builds `EnvMistralOcrClient` -> `ocr_markdown()` posts to Mistral/effective base

impact.why: A provider-specific credential and document content can be sent to a recipient that the accepted declaration did not authorize.

likelihood.why: The configuration is local and operator-mediated, and ordinary online, credential, media, and budget gates still apply.

limitations: This does not create an inbound public attack surface.
The operator controls device-local configuration in normal use.
An intentionally matching `MISTRAL_API_BASE` can avoid recipient drift, but it is not derived from the accepted target.

reachability.attacker: unintended lower-trust external recipient, or a lower-trust launcher when it can influence ambient Mistral base configuration
reachability.entrypoint: accepted markdown adapter declaration plus ordinary online markdown execution
reachability.outcome: wrong-recipient disclosure of the markdown credential and document bytes
preconditions: A non-Mistral or command/offline markdown target is accepted.
The declaration includes or resolves a bearer credential.
Online execution and budget gates allow the markdown job.
reachability.summary: The route is operator-mediated and requires a local declaration, resolvable credential, online opt-in, eligible document, and later markdown invocation.

attackPath.summary: An operator configures a markdown declaration for a non-Mistral URL or command with a credential reference. KCS accepts that declaration, drops the target during projection, and later sends the credential and eligible document through the fixed Mistral/effective-base client after ordinary online gates.

codeEvidence.explanation: `tools.toml` entries can include execution target fields and an authentication reference in the same accepted markdown declaration.
codeEvidence.label: tools.toml accepts markdown target and auth fields

codeEvidence.explanation: The runtime declaration has no place to carry `kind`, `cmd`, `args`, or `url`, so accepted target intent cannot reach dispatch.
codeEvidence.label: DeclaredAdapter omits execution target fields

codeEvidence.explanation: `declared_adapter_for_role()` preserves the declared credential and model while discarding the accepted command or URL recipient.
codeEvidence.label: Projection copies only model and auth from entries

codeEvidence.explanation: The production path consults the retained model but instantiates the fixed Mistral OCR client rather than dispatching to the declared target.
codeEvidence.label: Production markdown execution constructs Mistral OCR

codeEvidence.explanation: The destination is `MISTRAL_API_BASE` or the hard-coded Mistral default, while the credential can still come from the markdown declaration.
codeEvidence.label: Mistral client chooses ambient or default base URL

codeEvidence.explanation: Once ordinary online gates allow execution, the fixed/effective Mistral recipient receives both the resolved credential and document bytes.
codeEvidence.label: OCR request sends the file bytes with bearer authentication

codeEvidence.explanation: The preview is generic and does not expose that the accepted declared target and the effective Mistral recipient differ.
codeEvidence.label: Preview does not show declared or effective recipient

regressionTests: Assert a markdown declaration with `url` or `cmd` is rejected when custom markdown dispatch is unsupported.
If custom dispatch is supported, assert the exact declared URL or command reaches the executor.
Assert preview and approval display and bind the effective recipient.
Assert changing recipient identity changes the approval/provenance identity rather than reusing a model/auth-only profile.
Assert no credential is resolved for a declaration whose execution target is ignored.
remediation.summary: Reject unsupported markdown execution target fields at configuration load, or preserve `kind`, `cmd`, `args`, and `url` through runtime dispatch and bind the final recipient to preview, approval, credential resolution, profile identity, and request execution.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that an accepted adapter target and its credential must describe the same execution recipient. `tools.toml` validation accepts target fields, but `DeclaredAdapter` and `declared_adapter_for_role()` drop them while retaining `auth` and `model`. The production catalog therefore has no declared recipient to dispatch to and instantiates the fixed Mistral OCR client.

summary: KCS accepts markdown adapter declarations containing execution target fields such as `kind`, `cmd`, `args`, and `url`, but projects the runtime declaration down to `tool_id`, `model`, and `auth`. Production markdown execution then constructs the fixed Mistral OCR client, resolves the retained declared credential, and uploads document bytes to `MISTRAL_API_BASE` or `https://api.mistral.ai` rather than the accepted target.
title: Accepted markdown adapter targets are discarded before fixed Mistral execution

assertions: `kind`, `cmd`, `args`, and `url` are accepted configuration fields for adapter entries.
`DeclaredAdapter` and `declared_adapter_for_role()` do not preserve those target fields.
The production markdown path constructs `EnvMistralOcrClient` and uses only the retained model from the declaration.
`EnvMistralOcrClient` resolves the markdown credential and posts document bytes to its ambient/default OCR base URL.
limitations: No live OCR request or loopback capture was run.
No real credential or real document was used.
The prevalence of non-Mistral declarations in deployments was not measured.
validation.method: static source trace plus local/offline source invariant PoC
validation.summary: The source trace confirms accepted target fields, lossy projection, fixed Mistral dispatch, retained credential resolution, and bearer-authenticated document upload. The included PoC rechecked those invariants against the pinned revision without network access or credentials.
